Name: Baphuon
Description: Baphuon is an 11th-century temple-mountain with a 200 m raised walkway; it was taken apart by French archaeologists and rebuilt like a giant jigsaw, and its west side forms a huge reclining Buddha. Behind it in the forest sit Preah Palilay, a lonely tree-shaded sanctuary, and Tep Pranam, a large seated Buddha still used by nuns and worshippers.

Name: Angkor Balloon
Description: A tethered helium balloon rises about 200 m and stays up for 10-15 minutes. From the basket you see Angkor Wat's five towers and moat, Phnom Bakheng and the forest stretching to the horizon.

Name: Angkor Thom South Gate (wall walk)
Description: The 8 m-high earth wall around Angkor Thom has a shaded path on top that you can walk or cycle. Along it are the small Prasat Chrung corner shrines, and the far-less-visited North Gate, Victory Gate and Gate of the Dead, each topped with giant stone faces.

Name: East Mebon
Description: A 10th-century (953 AD) Hindu temple-mountain that once stood on an island in the middle of the East Baray, a 7 km reservoir that is now rice fields. Life-size stone elephants stand at the corners of its terraces, and five brick towers crown the top.

Name: Phnom Krom
Description: A 140 m hill crowned by three late-9th-century sandstone towers and a working pagoda. From the top you look over the Tonle Sap lake, flooded fields and stilt villages, and the sun sets over the water.

Name: Terrace of the Elephants
Description: The long royal viewing terrace with its parade of carved elephants, and the Terrace of the Leper King beside it. The real secret is the narrow trench between the outer wall and an older inner wall, where you walk past rows of deeply cut, almost untouched carvings of nagas, kings, apsaras and sea creatures.

Name: Kampot
Description: Kampot is a sleepy riverside town of faded French shophouses, sunset river cruises and Kampot pepper farms. Above it, Bokor Mountain holds an abandoned 1920s French hill station with a ghostly church and palace hotel; nearby Kep is a seaside village known for crab fresh from the market and boats to Rabbit Island.

Name: Phnom Kulen National Park
Description: The mountain where Jayavarman II declared the Khmer Empire in 802 AD. Visit carved riverbed lingas, the 16th-century reclining Buddha on top of a boulder at Preah Ang Thom, and swim at the two-level waterfall; with a motorbike guide you can reach forest-covered temples like Prasat Rong Chen.

Name: Quad Adventure Cambodia
Description: Guided rides on red dirt tracks through rice paddies, stilt-house villages and small pagodas, ending with sunset over the fields. Options run from 1.5-hour quad loops to half-day dirt-bike rides further out.

Name: Ta Som
Description: A small late-12th-century temple of Jayavarman VII with Bayon-style face towers on its gates. The famous sight is the eastern gate, almost swallowed by a huge strangler fig. Inside are quiet, crumbling galleries with well-kept devata carvings.
